plain: In the early 1950s, Michels says, an FBI field agent in Washington named Guy Hottel was building a dossier on the physicist Edward Condon, and Condon then lost his Q clearance, a high-level clearance for nuclear secrets. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, without naming a source for the investigation. In one he calls the loss of clearance "mysterious," dates it to 1953, and ties it instead to J. Robert Oppenheimer and the Los Alamos Primer, a 1943 Los Alamos Laboratory document.
